condition: Umbilical hernia in cirrhosis with ascites
summary: 57-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B), tense ascites and a large umbilical hernia with thin, shiny skin. Risk of rupture (Flood syndrome) and high peri-operative risk: ascites control and hepatology input before (or with) repair; Child-Pugh/MELD.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Swollen tummy and a large lump at the belly button
inputs.hpi: Known alcohol-related cirrhosis, abstinent 8 months. Tummy swelling increasing over 6 weeks despite tablets. Belly-button lump has grown and the skin over it is thin and shiny; no leakage of fluid. Not confused. No fever.

exam.general: Mild jaundice, spider naevi, palmar erythema. No asterixis.
exam.abdomen: Tense ascites with shifting dullness. 5 cm umbilical hernia, reducible with difficulty, overlying skin thin, shiny and stretched, no ulceration or leak. Splenomegaly.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Cirrhotic liver, splenomegaly, large-volume ascites. Umbilical defect 3 cm containing fluid and omentum.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Umbilical hernia with tense refractory ascites in Child-Pugh B cirrhosis; skin thinning (risk of rupture)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Umbilical hernia in decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) with tense diuretic-refractory ascites; thin shiny skin — risk of rupture. Hepatology review for ascites control (paracentesis/TIPS) and optimisation before repair; urgent surgery if leak, ulceration or incarceration.

redFlags.note: Thin shiny skin over an umbilical hernia with tense ascites: rupture risk must be surfaced.
Peri-operative mortality depends on liver function; the risk must be visible.

mustInclude.note: Repair without controlling ascites risks leak, recurrence and peritonitis; hepatology co-management is standard.

mustExclude.note: Day-case repair is inappropriate in decompensated cirrhosis.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: computeClinicalPrompts fires the hernia pathway for any CC/exam containing "hernia", "inguinal" or "umbilical", and always attaches the adult "LAPAROSCOPIC INGUINAL HERNIA REPAIR (TAPP)" operative plan. Its post-operative orders include day-case discharge.

guideline.name: EHS/AHS guidelines — treatment of umbilical and epigastric hernias
guideline.section: Indication for repair; mesh vs suture by defect size; open preperitoneal flat mesh; patients with liver cirrhosis and ascites
guideline.citation: Henriksen NA, Montgomery A, Kaufmann R, et al. Guidelines for treatment of umbilical and epigastric hernias from the European Hernia Society and Americas Hernia Society. Br J Surg. 2020;107:171–190.

guideline.name: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines — decompensated cirrhosis
guideline.section: Ascites management (diuretics, large-volume paracentesis); umbilical hernia in patients with ascites (ascites control before repair; risk of rupture)
guideline.citation: European Association for the Study of the Liver. EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines for the management of patients with decompensated cirrhosis. J Hepatol. 2018;69:406–460.

rationale: Permutation: comorbidity that changes management. Same hernia type; the plan must be driven by the liver disease and ascites (rupture risk, Child-Pugh/MELD, hepatology, ascites control).
